notes.heading: Overview of Cellular Respiration
notes.body: Cells break down glucose to make ATP. Overall equation: C6H12O6 + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy. Eukaryotes get roughly 30-32 ATP per glucose.

source.quote: Big picture: cells break down glucose to make ATP. Overall equation: C6H12O6 + 6 O2 -> 6 CO2 + 6 H2O + energy. Eukaryotes get roughly 30-32 ATP per glucose (older textbooks say 36-38

notes.heading: Glycolysis
notes.body: Happens in the cytoplasm. Does NOT need oxygen. Glucose (6 carbons) is split into 2 pyruvate (3 carbons each). Uses 2 ATP early on and makes 4 ATP, so the net gain is 2 ATP, plus 2 NADH.

source.quote: 1. Glycolysis - Happens in the cytoplasm. Does NOT need oxygen. - Glucose (6 carbons) is split into 2 pyruvate (3 carbons each). - Uses 2 ATP early on and makes 4 ATP, so the net gain is 2 ATP, plus 2 NADH

notes.heading: Pyruvate Oxidation
notes.body: Pyruvate enters the mitochondrial matrix. Each pyruvate becomes acetyl-CoA, releasing 1 CO2 and making 1 NADH.

source.quote: 2. Pyruvate oxidation - Pyruvate enters the mitochondrial matrix. - Each pyruvate becomes acetyl-CoA, releasing 1 CO2 and making 1 NADH

notes.heading: Krebs Cycle
notes.body: In the mitochondrial matrix. Acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to make citrate. Per glucose (two turns of the cycle): 2 ATP, 6 NADH, 2 FADH2 and 4 CO2.

source.quote: 3. Krebs cycle (citric acid cycle) - In the mitochondrial matrix. Acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to make citrate. - Per glucose (two turns of the cycle): 2 ATP, 6 NADH, 2 FADH2 and 4 CO2

notes.heading: Electron Transport Chain + Chemiosmosis
notes.body: On the inner mitochondrial membrane. NADH and FADH2 hand their electrons to protein complexes. Energy from the electrons pumps H+ across the membrane, building a proton gradient. H+ flows back through ATP synthase, which makes most of the ATP (about 26-28 per glucose). Oxygen is the final electron acceptor and ends up as water.

source.quote: 4. Electron transport chain + chemiosmosis - On the inner mitochondrial membrane. NADH and FADH2 hand their electrons to protein complexes. - Energy from the electrons pumps H+ across the membrane, building a proton gradient. - H+ flows…

notes.heading: Fermentation
notes.body: Glycolysis can keep going if NAD+ is regenerated. Lactic acid fermentation (muscle cells): pyruvate -> lactate. Alcohol fermentation (yeast): pyruvate -> ethanol + CO2. Only the 2 ATP from glycolysis per glucose.

source.quote: 5. No oxygen? Fermentation - Glycolysis can keep going if NAD+ is regenerated. - Lactic acid fermentation (muscle cells): pyruvate -> lactate. - Alcohol fermentation (yeast): pyruvate -> ethanol + CO2. - Only the 2 ATP from glycolysis per…

notes.heading: Exam Traps
notes.body: Most ATP comes from the electron transport chain, not from glycolysis or the Krebs cycle. CO2 is released in pyruvate oxidation and in the Krebs cycle: 6 CO2 per glucose in total. The water in the overall equation is made at the end of the electron transport chain, not in glycolysis.

quiz.explanation: Glycolysis uses 2 ATP and produces 4 ATP, resulting in a net gain of 2 ATP.
